content: The dietary recommendations for individuals with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), as outlined by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), emphasize the importance of achieving an energy deficit. These guidelines are similar to those provided for individuals with diabetes and obesity who do not have NAFLD. A critical aspect of these recommendations is the reduction of overall macronutrient intake. Specifically, individuals are advised to limit their consumption of saturated fats, starchy foods, and added sugars. Adopting healthier dietary patterns is strongly encouraged, with the Mediterranean diet being particularly supported by scientific evidence. This diet has been shown to improve both liver health and cardiometabolic outcomes. In addition to dietary changes, engaging in regular physical activity is recommended. Both aerobic exercise and resistance training have been demonstrated to positively impact NAFLD outcomes. The degree of improvement is influenced by the individual’s level of adherence to the treatment plan and the intensity of the exercise program.
